steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Physical theatre: the body is the primary means of expression — movement communicates meaning beyond words. | Key Fact: Frantic Assembly's chair work: using chairs as the central prop — creates dynamic, rhythmic, often aggressive sequences. | Key Fact: Push hands: two performers pushing against each other's hands — creates tension, balance and relational dynamics. | Key Fact: Lift and lean: one performer supports another's weight — requires trust, shows relationship and dependency.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe three Frantic Assembly techniques and explain the dramatic effect each can create. | How can physical theatre communicate emotions and relationships more effectively than dialogue alone? | You are creating a devised piece about conflict. How would you use physical theatre techniques to explore this theme?
